content: 1. Reduce the dose of olaparib to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) taken orally twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 3. Both erythromycin lactobionate and ondansetron prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when used with other QT-prolonging medications, electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure (CHF), or bradyarrhythmias. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 5. Both oxaliplatin and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Both erythromycin lactobionate and panobinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with other QT-prolonging drugs. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 11. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Both perphenazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pexidartinib dose. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Additionally, erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of pitavastatin, potentially increasing the risk of myopathy due to OATP1B1 inhibition. 18. Both erythromycin lactobionate and pitolisant prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while prednisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate and pretomanid both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 24. Both primaquine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Both prochlorperazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Both promazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Both promethazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of protamine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Both protriptyline and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transport. Co-administration is not recommended. 39. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of rifabutin by decreasing its metabolism, while rifabutin decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while ritonavir increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate. This combination is contraindicated. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous selumetinib dose. 49. Both sevoflurane and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both siponimod and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both solifenacin and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If use is unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 55. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1 transport. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both sunitinib and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both tacrolimus and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For daily use, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day. For as-needed use, limit to 10 mg every 72 hours. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 60. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per the drug monograph. 61. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 63. Both tetrabenazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Both thioridazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 67. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 68. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 69. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 70. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid co-administration with P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 71. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of toremifene by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of toremifene with QT-prolonging agents should be avoided. If co-administration is required, interrupt toremifene therapy. If interruption is not possible, closely monitor the patient, including obtaining ECGs for high-risk individuals. 72. Both trazodone and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
